faq.q: Why do my feet matter for writing?
faq.a: Flat feet keep your body steady. When your body is steady, your arm and hand can move smoothly.
A small tilt lets your arm move in a natural way, so writing feels easier and you can see your words.

faq.q: Why do I shake my hands before writing?
faq.a: Shaking and wiggling wakes up your hand muscles and helps them feel loose and ready.

faq.q: What if my feet do not touch the floor?
faq.a: Put a box, a step or a pile of books under them. A teacher or grown-up can help set it up.
asks: My feet do not reach the floor

faq.q: Which way should a left-handed writer tilt the paper?
faq.a: Tilt the top of the paper to the right. That helps you see what you write and keeps your hand from smudging it.

facts: Right-handed writers often tilt the top of the paper a little to the left, and left-handed writers tilt it to the right.
Sitting with both feet supported helps keep the body steady for writing.

quiz.say: Where should your feet be when you write?
quiz.why: Flat feet keep your body steady.

wrong.1: Feet on the desk would make it hard to sit and write.
wrong.2: Swinging feet make your body wobble. A footrest can help.

quiz.say: What does your helper hand do?
quiz.show: What does your helper hand do?
quiz.why: Your helper hand stops the paper sliding away.

wrong.1: Snacks can wait. Your helper hand has a writing job.
wrong.2: Waving does not help. Your helper hand holds the paper.
